page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs consisting of 24 physical cores with hyper-threading operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor includes 105 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. The server is equipped with 96.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 9 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results highlight strong performance across compute, memory, and specialized workloads. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 19030.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 65056.32, indicating robust parallel processing capabilities. Memory performance is notable, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 222.1 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 95.0 GB/sec, both placing in the strong tier. The hardware-assisted matrix extensions contribute to high efficiency in machine learning tasks; for instance, LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model reached a top-tier speed of 353.0 tokens/sec, while a medium 7B model achieved 30.87 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7i-flex family offers a balanced resource density for compute-heavy workloads that do not require the full sustained performance of standard c7i instances. The 1 to 2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio optimizes compute resources while keeping memory overhead low, making it a cost-effective choice for CPU-bound tasks. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all disk operations must traverse the network, which may introduce latency for I/O-heavy applications. Additionally, the absence of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for massive parallel training, though the onboard Intel AMX instructions partially offset this for smaller inference workloads.

This instance is well-suited for compute-intensive applications such as software compilation, where it scored 45495.0 on Geekbench clang compilation, and high-throughput web serving, demonstrated by a static web serving throughput of 72.85 GB/sec. It is also highly capable for database operations, processing 62.18 million Redis SET operations per second, and running medium-scale machine learning inference, data compression, and general-purpose batch processing.
